# Example: Python + uv + tox (with `.tox` extends and schedule-gated matrix)

**Source**: generated by the skill from a fresh clone of [`pallets/click`](https://github.com/pallets/click) on 2026-05-22, with no pre-existing `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

Where `python-uv-tox/` shows the basic Python+uv shape, this one shows what happens when a project has a more elaborate tox configuration (style, type checking, docs in addition to tests).

## Patterns this example demonstrates

- **Hidden `.tox` job with `extends:` reuse across 4 callers** (lint, test, typing, docs). Beats copy-pasting `uv tool install tox --with tox-uv` four times.
- **Schedule-gated full matrix**: `test` runs Python 3.13 on every push; the full 3.10-3.14 matrix lives on `test-matrix` and only fires when `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"`. Every-push pipelines stay fast; nightly schedules exercise the full grid.
- **`workflow:rules:`** blocks the duplicate branch + MR pipeline once an MR opens (the classic gotcha for new GitLab users).
- **`needs: []` on every test-stage job** so the DAG starts the test stage in parallel with build.
- **Deploy stub** gated to both `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` and `$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH`, both manual.

## YAML files

- `.gitlab-ci.yml`: Workflow 1 (Create initial pipeline) capture.

## Reproducing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pallets/click /tmp/click
cd /tmp/click
rm -rf .gitlab-ci.yml .gitlab .github/workflows
```

Then in a fresh Claude Code (or other AI editor) session, prompt:

> Set up GitLab CI for this repo.

Compare the agent's output to the YAML in this directory. They should match in shape; small differences are expected (component versions, comments).
